_doc: The storyteller (sim/storyteller): one director paces everything that befalls the district you are in, instead of a flat chance per dawn. A teller is picked at New game (tellers[0] by default). Its tale moves through phases (calm, rising, peak, ebb; the Gale has one: wild); each phase lasts days[lo,hi], fires an incident with `chance` per dawn (never within minGap days of the last), and draws its kind from `kinds` weights: everyday = the happenings table (data/systems/events.json), boon / omen / twist / threat = an incident below, arc = a chain. Threats cost points (income per dawn grows with the day and with what you own) and raise tension; no threat fires while tension is over tensionCap, and a merciful teller holds threats back while your spark is low or your town is deep in despair. Nothing repeats: an incident waits out its cooldown, and one told lately is weighed down (novelty). Incident ops: despair {add}; food {days} (days of the town's appetite, + or -); stock {mul}; flame {add, share, pick: lit|unlit|any}; spark {add} and coin / item (only when you are in that town); route {break|mend}; settle (a wanderer stays for good); feud {add} (with a neighbouring district); happening {id}; pressure {family, need} (packs of that family gather near the town until you rout `need` of them). `intensity` scales losses and need. An incident with `days` stays in force that long and shows on the board's Tidings page (`board`, {left} = days left, {need} = packs left); `resolve.by` rout (kill packs near the town) or when (a happening-world clause holds at the deadline) decides between `win` and `lose` ops and lines. Lines are spoken by a resident ({name}); {town} the town, {other} a neighbouring district.

tellers.name: Old Ember
tellers.title: the hearth-keeper
tellers.blurb: Trouble builds, breaks, and passes. After every storm, a quiet spell to mend in. The way most tales go.

tellers.name: The Weaver
tellers.title: who takes her time
tellers.blurb: Long quiet seasons to build in. Then one thread pulled all the way through. Fewer tales, and each one a chapter.

tellers.name: The Gale
tellers.title: that asks no leave
tellers.blurb: No rhythm, no mercy, no pattern. Windfalls and wolves in the same week. For those who have seen the other tales.

phaseLines.calm: The roads are quiet. A good time to build something.
phaseLines.rising: Folk keep looking at the tree line. Something is on its way.
phaseLines.peak: Trouble is here, or near enough to smell.
phaseLines.ebb: The worst has passed. People are counting what is left.
phaseLines.wild: Nobody will say what tomorrow brings. Nobody ever could.

incidents.name: Bandit Raid
say: They came at dusk and took what they liked. They are camped out past the fields, {name} says, laughing about it.
Raiders. Half the stores gone, and they have not even bothered to run far.
news: Bandits raided {town} in the night. {name} says they are still camped nearby.
{name} woke the lane: raiders hit {town}'s stores and are sitting just outside it.
incidents.board: Raiders are camped outside {town}. Rout {need} more of their packs and the stores come back. They strike again in {left} days.

winLines: The raiders have scattered. {name} is already carting the stores back to {town}.
{town} got its own back. {name} says they will think twice now.
loseLines: The raiders came back to {town} for the rest. Nobody stood in their way.
{name} says the bandits took a second helping from {town}, and left when they were ready.

incidents.name: Wolves at the Fences
say: Wolves in the sheep pens again. Nobody will go out to the far field.
{name} counted seven of them at the fence last night. Bold as you like.
news: Wolves are taking stock at {town}. {name} says the far fields are abandoned.
A pack has come down on {town}; {name} lost two ewes to it.
incidents.board: A wolf pack is working the fields round {town}. Rout {need} more packs and the herders go back out ({left} days).

winLines: The wolves are gone from {town}. {name} left hides on your step by way of thanks.
loseLines: The wolves took what they wanted from {town} and moved on fat.

incidents.name: The Grey Tide
say: There are things at the edge of the fields that were not there yesterday. Grey things. They just stand.
{name} will not go past the last house. Says the hollow ones are gathering.
news: A grey tide has come in round {town}: hollow things at the field edge, and the hearths burning low.
{name} says the despair-born are thick outside {town}, and people can feel it indoors.
incidents.board: The grey tide stands outside {town}; its hearths sink while it does. Rout {need} more packs of the despair-born to break it ({left} days).

winLines: The tide broke at {town}. {name} says people came out and stood in the lane, just breathing.
Whatever stood outside {town} is gone. The hearths are drawing again.
loseLines: The grey tide did not break. It settled into {town}, and people let it.
{name} says nobody fought it. {town} just got quieter.

incidents.name: Blight
say: The crop has gone black at the root. All of it, in a week.
{name} pulled a whole row and every one was rotten.
news: Blight took the fields at {town}. {name} says the stores will not see them through.
The crop failed at {town}; people are already eating less.
incidents.board: Blight took {town}'s crop. If its stores hold two days of food when {left} days are up, it comes through. Bring food, or send a convoy.

winLines: {town} came through the blight fed. {name} says people know who carried the grain in.
Nobody starved at {town}. There is a kind of pride in the place this morning.
loseLines: {town} went hungry after the blight. {name} says some doors have not opened since.
The stores ran out at {town}. People remember who had grain and who did not.

incidents.name: Road Washed Out
say: The road went in the night. A cart could not get through now.
{name} walked out to look. Says half the hill is sitting on the road.
news: A road out of {town} has washed out. Carts are turning back.
{name} says the road by {town} is gone under mud; it wants stone, timber and hands.

incidents.name: An Envoy Slighted
say: The envoy from {other} left without eating. That is not a small thing, where they come from.
{name} heard shouting from the hall. The envoy from {other} rode out before dawn.
news: An envoy from {other} left {town} insulted. {name} says the seat will hear of it.
There are hard words between {town} and {other} this morning.

incidents.name: Deserters
say: Two came in off the road with army boots and no army. They want work and no questions.
{name} has put the strangers up in the barn. Deserters, by the look.
news: Two deserters have settled at {town}. {name} says they work hard and flinch at horns.
{town} has two new pairs of hands this morning, and nobody is asking where from.

incidents.name: A Wanderer Stays
say: Someone walked in last night and asked if there was an empty house. There are plenty of those.
{name} says the newcomer has a way of whistling. People keep stopping to listen.
news: A wanderer has decided to stay at {town}. {name} says they came in already lit.
{town} has a new face this morning, and a new light in a window that was dark.

incidents.name: Bumper Harvest
say: I have never seen the carts come in so full. We will have to build a second crib.
{name} keeps going out to look at the granary, just to look.
news: The harvest came in heavy at {town}. {name} says there is more than the stores will hold.
{town} has grain to spare this morning, and people are almost cheerful about it.

incidents.name: Trade Fair
say: Carts from three roads, all at once. The square has not been this loud in years.
{name} sold everything by noon and stood about grinning like a fool.
news: A fair has sprung up at {town}: traders from every road. {name} says the shelves are full.
{town} is loud this morning. A fair came in with the carts.

incidents.name: A Carrier's Cache
say: We found this under the old hearthstone. It is warm. It has been waiting, I think, for one of you.
{name} dug it up mending the wall. Says it belongs with whoever carries the spark now.
news: {name} found something an old spark-carrier buried at {town}, and has left it at your door.
A cache from one who walked before you turned up at {town}. {name} thought you should have it.

incidents.name: The Road Gang
say: They went out with mallets and no one asked them to. First time in my life.
{name} says the young ones mended the road for something to do. Imagine that.
news: Folk from {town} mended their road unasked. {name} says carts are through again.
The road by {town} was mended overnight by its own people.

incidents.name: The Hairy Star
say: A star with a tail, three nights running. My grandmother would have had the shutters nailed.
{name} says it means a death. {name} says that about everything.
news: A tailed star hangs over {town}. {name} says nothing good follows one.
People at {town} were up all night watching the sky.

incidents.name: The Birds Leave
say: The rooks have gone from the elms. All of them, in one morning. That is not right.
{name} noticed first: no birds. You do not hear how quiet it is until someone says.
news: The birds have left {town}. {name} says the old folk are stacking wood early.
No birdsong at {town} this morning. People keep stopping to listen for it.

incidents.name: Cut Purses
say: Third purse cut this week, and always on the road, never in town. Someone is counting our carts.
{name} says there are strangers watching the road and writing things down.
news: Travellers near {town} are being robbed, a little at a time. {name} says someone is taking the town's measure.
{name} was followed on the road to {town}.

incidents.name: Tribute
say: They did not even draw steel this time. They sent a list.
{name} carried our tribute out to them. I could not look.
news: {town} is paying tribute to the bandit king. {name} says it will be every season now.
The bandits own {town}'s road, and {town} knows it.

incidents.name: The King's Fall
say: They say the bandit king's own men left him in the night, after what you did. The road is ours.
{name} is hanging lanterns. Lanterns! For a road.
news: The bandit king's band has broken up. {town} is lighting lanterns along its road.
{name} says the roads round {town} are free, and that it was your doing.

incidents.name: The Long Frost
say: The ground is like iron and it is not even midwinter. We are into the seed grain already.
{name} is burning fence rails. That is how you know.
news: A killing frost has settled on {town}. {name} says the stores are going twice as fast.
{town} woke to ice on the inside of the shutters.
incidents.board: The long frost holds {town}. If its stores hold two days of food when it lifts in {left} days, it comes through. Bring food, fuel a convoy, or share your own.

winLines: The frost broke and {town} is still standing, every house of it. {name} is calling it the winter nobody was left out.
{town} came through the frost whole. There is to be a feast.
loseLines: The frost lifted too late for {town}. {name} says they are counting who is left.
{town} came out of the frost thinner and quieter, and not all of it came out.

incidents.name: Pilgrims on the Road
say: Pilgrims, a dozen of them, walking to the place where the last spark-carrier rested. They sang the whole way in.
{name} gave them the barn. One has decided not to leave.
news: Pilgrims came through {town}, following the old spark-carriers' road. One has stayed.
{name} says the pilgrims at {town} are asking after you.

incidents.name: The Shrine Lit
say: They lit the old shrine. It has not burned in my lifetime. You can see it from the mill.
{name} stood by it all night. Says it is the same fire you carry. I believe it.
news: The pilgrims lit the old shrine at {town}. {name} says half the town sat up with it.
A fire is burning at {town}'s shrine this morning, for the first time in living memory.

incidents.name: The First Cough
say: There is a cough going round the carters. It sounds wet. I do not like it.
{name} has shut the children in. Says it started like this the last time.
news: A cough is going round at {town}. {name} is keeping well back from the well.
{town} is uneasy this morning: two carters are abed and grey in the face.

incidents.name: The Grey Cough
say: It is in every third house now. People have stopped answering their doors.
{name} is nursing four of them. Nobody is nursing {name}.
news: The grey cough has hold of {town}. {name} says doors are shut all down the lane.
Sickness at {town}: the hearths are untended and the lane is empty.
incidents.board: The grey cough has {town}. If half its hearths are lit when it passes in {left} days, it will remember who sat with the sick. Keep its people burning.

winLines: The cough has passed at {town}, and nobody sat it out alone. {name} says that is your doing.
{town} came through the grey cough with its fires in. People are saying your name kindly.
loseLines: The cough has burned itself out at {town}. What it left is very quiet.
{name} says the sickness is over at {town}. Nobody is celebrating.

arcs.name: The Bandit King
arcs.blurb: A band is taking the town's measure. Break them when they come, or pay them forever.

arcs.name: The Ashen Winter
arcs.blurb: The birds leave first. Then the frost comes for the stores.

arcs.name: The Pilgrim Road
arcs.blurb: They walk where the spark-carriers walked. Lately that means here.

arcs.name: The Grey Cough
arcs.blurb: A wet cough among the carters. Then every third house.
